content: Community Health Workers (CHWs) are individuals who are deeply trusted within the communities they serve. They act as a critical bridge between healthcare systems and populations that are often underserved or marginalized. Their responsibilities encompass a wide range of activities, including conducting outreach efforts to engage community members, advocating for the needs and rights of individuals within the community, providing social support to those in need, delivering health education to promote awareness and understanding, and facilitating referrals to appropriate healthcare services. In certain situations, CHWs may also carry out specific, limited clinical tasks, but only under the direct supervision of licensed healthcare professionals.
